claims.statement: The tutorial recommends committing code and configuration so future codespaces from the repository can reuse the configuration and customizations. In its template-created case no hosted repository yet contains the code, and publishing the current branch can create one. Availability of committed customization does not prove successful installation, identical runtime environments or remote custody without a verified push; publication is not authorized by this source.

Creating through a template repository's Use this template button offers no configuration choice and uses the default .devcontainer/devcontainer.json or root .devcontainer.json. This entry-point-specific rule does not mean every creation flow lacks a choice, nor prove either configuration is safe or effective.

The fragment describes directly connecting to a codespace through the editor and links further instructions. It does not establish connection prerequisites, permissions or a successful live connection.

The support fragment is a conditional escalation suggestion whose antecedent depends on surrounding content. It links a separate support workflow; it does not mandate contacting support, authorize disclosure of logs or prove a support case was submitted.

The branch procedure optionally enables the source-control status-bar display, selects the branch name and either switches to an existing branch or creates a named one. Captions are textual evidence only; no branch was switched or created and no remote protection or synchronization behavior is verified.

After account connection to the Codespaces extension, the editor creation procedure selects a repository, displays who will pay in later prompts, selects a branch, optionally chooses a dev container configuration and chooses a machine. Included Remote Explorer and machine-availability fragments and marketplace link remain separate dependencies. Example repository/payer names are not operational targets; a payer prompt is not cost approval or actual billing evidence.

Codespace customization can adjust vCPUs/RAM, dotfiles and installed tools/scripts. Repositories may provide multiple devcontainer.json configurations. At launch the chosen configuration and dependent files drive tool/runtime installation and setup, so these files are potentially executable inputs rather than inert proof of a safe environment. No installation, resource change or setup was performed; linked customization and dev-container documentation remain separate.

The default-image fragment points to an external devcontainers/images universal-image directory for contents. It does not enumerate packages, pin that moving branch or verify the actual installed image and tool versions.
